newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Central Bank trends down Philippine peso at close.
newsitem.headline: Central Bank trends down Philippine peso at close.

text.p: * Central Bank raises buying rate to 26.366 to dollar
The Philippine Central Bank steadily raised its dollar buying rate throughout the session which led the peso to close weaker at 26.366 to the dollar, traders said.
The peso closed at 26.363 on Tuesday.
"The Central Bank bought dollars from 26.364 to 26.366 throughout the day," one trader from a foreign bank said.
It was estimated the Central Bank bought about $40 million in the market.

"We believe that the Central Bank is buying back the dollars it sold in the past two weeks," the trader said. The Central Bank was selling dollars to curb the peso's weakening following the big sell-offs in the local equities market.

Another trader said the Central Bank was also preparing for a possible lowering of interest rates in the coming days after a series of rate increases to stop the fleeing dollars. The threat of a massive outflow has since abated.
The peso was wedged within a tight range of 26.363 and 26.266 on a turnover of $157.5 million.
